Title: Send Authorization Bearer header when a token is stored
Preconditions: sessionStorage key shopfloor.token = 'tok-abc'; fetch is mocked to resolve ok with {}
Steps:
1. Store the token in sessionStorage.
2. Call request('GET', '/auth/me').
3. Inspect the fetch arguments.
Expected Result: fetch is called with /api/auth/me and header Authorization = 'Bearer tok-abc'.

Title: Call the unauthorized handler on a 401 from a protected path
Preconditions: setUnauthorizedHandler(spy) registered; fetch mocked to return 401 with failures[0].rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'
Steps:
1. Register the spy handler.
2. Call request('GET', '/work-orders').
3. Await the rejection.
Expected Result: The spy is called once; the promise rejects with ApiError whose failures[0].rule is 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Call POST /auth/login with userId and password through authService.login
Preconditions: fetch mocked to return 200 with { token: 'tok-abc', tokenType: 'Bearer', expiresAt: '2026-10-30T11:15:30.000Z', user: { userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', role: 'supervisor', status: 'active' } }
Steps:
1. Call login('sup01', 'Correct-Horse-42').
2. Inspect the fetch arguments and the result.
Expected Result: fetch is called with /api/auth/login, method POST, Content-Type application/json and a JSON body holding only userId and password; the promise resolves with the response body.

Title: Call GET /auth/me through authService.getCurrentUser
Preconditions: Token 'tok-abc' stored; fetch mocked to return 200 { user: { userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', role: 'supervisor', status: 'active' } }
Steps:
1. Call getCurrentUser().
2. Inspect the fetch call and result.
Expected Result: fetch is called with /api/auth/me, method GET and the Bearer header; the promise resolves with the user body.

Title: Omit Authorization header when no token is stored
Preconditions: sessionStorage is empty; fetch mocked to resolve ok with {}
Steps:
1. Clear sessionStorage.
2. Call request('GET', '/health').
3. Inspect the fetch headers.
Expected Result: The fetch headers contain no Authorization key.

Title: Do not call the unauthorized handler on a 401 from /auth/login
Preconditions: Handler spy registered; token 'tok-old' stored; fetch mocked to return 401 with rule 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS'
Steps:
1. Call request for /auth/login.
2. Await the rejection.
3. Check the spy and sessionStorage.
Expected Result: The promise rejects with ApiError whose failures[0].rule is 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS'; the handler is not called; token 'tok-old' is still stored.

Title: Do not call the unauthorized handler on 403 or 429 responses
Preconditions: Handler spy registered; token 'tok-abc' stored; fetch mocked once with 403 rule 'FORBIDDEN' and once with 429 rule 'RATE_LIMITED'
Steps:
1. Trigger the 403 response and await the rejection.
2. Trigger the 429 response and await the rejection.
3. Check the spy and sessionStorage.
Expected Result: Both calls reject with ApiError carrying the server failures; the handler is never called; the token stays stored.

Title: Throw ApiError on a 401 when no unauthorized handler is registered
Preconditions: No handler registered (setUnauthorizedHandler never called or called with null); fetch mocked to return 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'
Steps:
1. Call request('GET', '/work-orders').
2. Await the rejection.
Expected Result: The promise rejects with ApiError (rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'); no TypeError is thrown.

Title: Keep the token out of the request URL and body
Preconditions: Token 'tok-abc' stored; fetch mocked to resolve ok
Steps:
1. Call request.
2. Inspect URL and body passed to fetch.
Expected Result: URL is exactly /api/work-orders and the body is the JSON of { name: 'WO-1' }; neither contains 'tok-abc'; the token appears only in the Authorization header.

Title: Show user name, role label and Logout for a supervisor
Preconditions: AuthProvider supplies status 'authenticated' and user { userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', role: 'supervisor', status: 'active' }
Steps:
1. Render AppShell inside the providers.
2. Read the header text.
Expected Result: The header shows 'Asha Rao' and 'Manufacturing Supervisor' and a Logout button; navigation is visible.

Title: Map operator and administrator roles to their display labels
Preconditions: Authenticated user once with role 'operator' and once with role 'administrator'
Steps:
1. Render AppShell as the operator.
2. Render AppShell as the administrator.
3. Read the role label each time.
Expected Result: The operator sees 'Shop-Floor Operator'; the administrator sees 'Administrator'.

Title: Clear token and return to /login on Logout
Preconditions: Authenticated as sup01; sessionStorage holds 'tok-abc'; fetch is spied
Steps:
1. Click Logout.
2. Inspect sessionStorage, location and fetch calls.
Expected Result: sessionStorage no longer has shopfloor.token; location is /login; AuthProvider status is 'anonymous'; no HTTP request is made on logout.

Title: Hide navigation, user name and Logout when anonymous
Steps:
1. Render AppShell as anonymous.
2. Query for navigation links, a user name and a Logout button.
Expected Result: No navigation, no user name and no Logout control are rendered.

Title: Restore the session from a stored token through GET /auth/me
Preconditions: Token 'tok-abc' stored; getCurrentUser mocked to resolve { user: { userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', role: 'supervisor', status: 'active' } }
Test Data: Render AuthProvider with a status probe
Steps:
1. Render AuthProvider.
2. Observe status over time.
Expected Result: Status is 'loading' first, then 'authenticated' with user.userId 'sup01'; getCurrentUser is called once.

Title: Store the token and set the user on login()
Preconditions: sessionStorage empty; authService.login mocked to resolve { token: 'tok-abc', tokenType: 'Bearer', expiresAt: '2026-10-30T11:15:30.000Z', user: sup01 }
Steps:
1. Render AuthProvider as anonymous.
2. Call login from the context.
3. Read status, user and storage.
Expected Result: sessionStorage shopfloor.token = 'tok-abc'; status 'authenticated'; user.userId 'sup01'.

Title: Clear token and status on logout() without a server call
Preconditions: Authenticated as sup01 with token 'tok-abc'; fetch spied
Steps:
1. Call logout from the context.
2. Read status and storage; inspect fetch calls.
Expected Result: Token removed; status 'anonymous'; user is null; fetch is not called.

Title: Register an unauthorized handler that ends the session
Preconditions: Authenticated as sup01 with token 'tok-abc'; fetch mocked to return 401 for GET /work-orders
Steps:
1. Render AuthProvider as authenticated.
2. Make the 401 call through apiClient.
3. Read status and storage.
Expected Result: Token cleared; status 'anonymous'; the call still rejects with ApiError.

Title: Clear the token when session restore fails with 401
Preconditions: Token 'tok-expired' stored; getCurrentUser mocked to reject with ApiError rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'
Steps:
1. Render AuthProvider.
2. Wait for status to settle.
Expected Result: Token removed from sessionStorage; status 'anonymous'; user is null.

Title: Propagate a login failure and keep the session anonymous
Preconditions: authService.login mocked to reject with ApiError rule 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS'; sessionStorage empty
Steps:
1. Call login and catch the error.
2. Read status and storage.
Expected Result: The caller receives ApiError with rule 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS'; no token stored; status stays 'anonymous'.

Title: Become anonymous immediately when no token is stored
Steps:
1. Render AuthProvider.
2. Read status on first render and after effects.
Expected Result: Status is 'anonymous' without passing through a network wait; getCurrentUser is never called.

Title: Report status 'loading' while the session restore is pending
Preconditions: Token stored; getCurrentUser returns a promise that is not yet resolved
Test Data: Render AuthProvider with a status probe
Steps:
1. Render AuthProvider.
2. Read status before resolving the promise.
Expected Result: Status is 'loading' and user is null until the promise settles.

Title: Clear the session when restore fails with a network error
Preconditions: Token stored; getCurrentUser mocked to reject with TypeError('Failed to fetch')
Steps:
1. Render AuthProvider.
2. Wait for status to settle.
Expected Result: Token removed; status 'anonymous'; no unhandled promise rejection is raised.

Title: Return token, tokenType, UTC expiresAt and public user on valid login
Preconditions: In-memory MongoDB; seed users sup01 (supervisor, active, 'Asha Rao') with password 'Correct-Horse-42'; config jwtExpiresIn '1h'
Steps:
1. Call authService.login.
2. Inspect the result and decode the token.
Expected Result: Result has token (JWT string), tokenType 'Bearer', expiresAt ISO-8601 UTC string ending in 'Z' and user { userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', role: 'supervisor', status: 'active' }.

Title: Return id, userId, name, role and status from getUserForToken
Preconditions: Active user sup01 exists; token from signToken('sup01', config)
Steps:
1. Sign a token for sup01.
2. Call getUserForToken.
Expected Result: Result is { id: <24-character hex string of the user _id>, userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', role: 'supervisor', status: 'active' } and has no passwordHash.

Title: Whitelist public fields in toPublicUser for documents and lean objects
Preconditions: A Mongoose document and a lean object for sup01, both carrying passwordHash
Steps:
1. Call toPublicUser with the document.
2. Call toPublicUser with the lean object.
Expected Result: Both results equal { userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', role: 'supervisor', status: 'active' } and contain no other key.

Title: Return the correct public role for each of the three roles
Test Data: login for sup01, op01 and adm01 with 'Correct-Horse-42'
Steps:
1. Log in as each user through authService.login.
2. Read user.role.
Expected Result: Roles returned are 'supervisor', 'operator' and 'administrator' respectively; each has status 'active'.

Title: Reject a wrong password with INVALID_CREDENTIALS
Steps:
1. Call authService.login.
2. Catch the error.
Expected Result: ValidationError status 401; failures[0] has rule 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS', message 'The user ID or password is incorrect.', fix 'Check your user ID and password and try again.'; no token is signed.

Title: Compare against a dummy hash for an unknown user ID
Preconditions: No user 'ghost01' exists; verifyPassword is spied
Steps:
1. Spy on verifyPassword.
2. Call authService.login.
3. Catch the error.
Expected Result: verifyPassword is called exactly once with a bcrypt-format dummy hash; the error is ValidationError 401 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS' identical to the wrong-password error.

Title: Reject an inactive user after a correct password with ACCOUNT_INACTIVE
Preconditions: Inactive user ina01 with password 'Correct-Horse-42'; signToken is spied
Steps:
1. Call authService.login.
2. Catch the error.
3. Check the signToken spy.
Expected Result: ValidationError status 403 with rule 'ACCOUNT_INACTIVE', message 'This account is deactivated.', fix 'Ask an Administrator to reactivate the account.'; signToken is not called.

Title: Hide the inactive status when the password is wrong
Steps:
1. Call authService.login.
2. Catch the error.
Expected Result: ValidationError status 401 with rule 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS'; the rule 'ACCOUNT_INACTIVE' is not used.

Title: Reject getUserForToken when the user no longer exists
Preconditions: Token signed for 'sup01'; user sup01 deleted from users
Steps:
1. Sign the token.
2. Delete the user document.
3. Call getUserForToken.
Expected Result: ValidationError status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject getUserForToken when the user is inactive
Preconditions: Token signed for ina01; ina01 status 'inactive'
Steps:
1. Sign a token for ina01.
2. Call getUserForToken.
Expected Result: ValidationError status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Skip the database lookup when the token is invalid
Steps:
1. Call getUserForToken with an invalid token.
2. Catch the error.
3. Check the findOne spy.
Expected Result: ValidationError 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'; User.findOne is never called.

Title: Create the dummy hash lazily once and cache it
Preconditions: Fresh module state; hashPassword spied; no users exist
Steps:
1. Call login for 'ghost01'.
2. Call login for 'ghost02'.
3. Count hashPassword calls.
Expected Result: Both reject with 401 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS'; hashPassword is called once in total for the dummy hash, with cost 12.

Title: Strip extra fields from toPublicUser
Preconditions: Object { _id, __v: 0, userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', role: 'supervisor', status: 'active', passwordHash: '$2a$04$x', createdAt, updatedAt }
Steps:
1. Call toPublicUser.
2. List the result keys.
Expected Result: Keys are exactly userId, name, role, status.

Title: Derive expiresAt from the token exp claim
Steps:
1. Freeze time.
2. Call login.
3. Compare expiresAt with the decoded exp.
Expected Result: expiresAt equals '2026-10-30T11:15:30.000Z' (exp * 1000 serialized with toISOString) and ends with 'Z'.

Title: Keep passwordHash out of the login result
Steps:
1. Call login.
2. Stringify the result.
Expected Result: The string contains no 'passwordHash', no '$2a$' and no '$2b$' fragment.

Title: Accept a valid Bearer token of an active user and set req.user
Preconditions: App built with createApp(extend, config); test-only route GET /api/test/whoami echoes req.user; token for sup01 from authHelpers
Steps:
1. Call GET /api/test/whoami with the header.
2. Read the body.
Expected Result: Status 200; req.user equals { id: <24-char hex>, userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', role: 'supervisor', status: 'active' }.

Title: Accept tokens for supervisor, operator and administrator
Steps:
1. Request /api/auth/me with the sup01 token.
2. Repeat with op01 and adm01.
Expected Result: Each call returns 200 with the matching user.role.

Title: Keep GET /api/health public
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/health with no header.
Expected Result: Status 200 and body { status: 'ok', timestamp: <ISO string> }.

Title: Keep POST /api/auth/login public
Test Data: POST /api/auth/login { userId: 'sup01', password: 'Correct-Horse-42' } with no Authorization header
Steps: 1. Send the request without a token.
Expected Result: Status 200 with a token in the body; no 401 is returned.

Title: Reject a request without an Authorization header
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/test/whoami.
Expected Result: Status 401; body { error: 'ValidationError', failures: [{ rule: 'UNAUTHENTICATED', message: 'A valid token is required.', fix: 'Sign in again.' }] }.

Title: Reject the Basic scheme
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/test/whoami with the Basic header.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'; the handler does not run.

Title: Reject an empty Bearer token
Steps:
1. Call the route with 'Bearer '.
2. Call the route with 'Bearer'.
Expected Result: Both calls return 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a header with extra parts
Preconditions: Test-only protected route; valid token T1 for sup01
Steps: 1. Call the route with the header.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a token that is not a JWT
Steps: 1. Call the route.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'; the response is not 500.

Title: Reject an expired token
Preconditions: Token for sup01 signed with the test secret and expiresIn '-1s'
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/auth/me.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a token with a tampered signature
Preconditions: Valid token for sup01; last 4 characters of the signature replaced with 'AAAA'
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/auth/me.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a token with alg none
Preconditions: Unsigned token with header alg 'none' and payload sub 'adm01'
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/auth/me.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'; no user is loaded.

Title: Reject a token signed with a different secret
Preconditions: Token for sup01 signed with the 32-character secret 'other-secret-other-secret-other-1'
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/auth/me.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a token issued before the user was deactivated
Preconditions: Active user sup01 with valid token; then status set to 'inactive' in the database
Steps:
1. Call /api/auth/me and confirm 200.
2. Set sup01 status to 'inactive'.
3. Call /api/auth/me again with the same token.
Expected Result: First call 200; second call 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a token for a user that no longer exists
Preconditions: Valid token for sup01; user document then deleted
Steps:
1. Delete sup01.
2. Call /api/auth/me with the token.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a token whose subject is an object before any query
Preconditions: Correctly signed token with payload { sub: { $ne: null } }; User.findOne spied
Steps:
1. Call GET /api/auth/me.
2. Check the findOne spy.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'; User.findOne is not called.

Title: Ignore a token passed in the query string or a cookie
Steps:
1. Call with the query parameter only.
2. Call with the cookie only.
Expected Result: Both calls return 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Return 401 for an unknown /api path without a token
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/nope with no Authorization header.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED' (not 404 NOT_FOUND).

Title: Require a token for every HTTP method on a protected route
Preconditions: Test-only route registered for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE with a call counter
Steps:
1. Call the route with each method.
2. Read the counter.
Expected Result: Every call returns 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'; the counter stays 0.

Title: Return the same 401 body for a missing token and a deactivated user's token
Preconditions: Token for ina01 (inactive); second request without header
Steps:
1. Call with the inactive user's token.
2. Call with no header.
3. Compare the bodies.
Expected Result: Both responses are status 401 with identical bodies (rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'); the cause is not disclosed.

Title: Return 404 NOT_FOUND for an unknown /api path with a valid token
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/nope.
Expected Result: Status 404 with rule 'NOT_FOUND'.

Title: Return 404 for a path outside /api without a token
Steps: 1. Call GET /nope.
Expected Result: Status 404 with rule 'NOT_FOUND'; no 401.

Title: Accept a token just before exp and reject it just after
Preconditions: Fake timers; token for sup01 with expiresIn '60s' issued at 2026-01-05T09:00:00Z
Steps:
1. Set the clock to 09:00:59Z and call.
2. Set the clock to 09:01:01Z and call.
Expected Result: First call 200; second call 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a header with trailing whitespace
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/auth/me.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED' (the header must match Bearer followed by one non-space token).

Title: Reject a 10,000 character token without a server error
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/auth/me.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'; not 500 and not 431.

Title: Reject a token with an empty string subject
Preconditions: Correctly signed token with payload { sub: '' }
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/auth/me.
Expected Result: Status 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED' (no user matches).

Title: Authenticate 20 parallel requests with the same token
Preconditions: Active user sup01 and one valid token
Steps:
1. Fire 20 requests in parallel with Promise.all.
2. Collect statuses and bodies.
Expected Result: All 20 responses are 200 with user.userId 'sup01'; no 401 or 500.

Title: Clarify whether the Bearer scheme is case-sensitive
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/auth/me with the lowercase scheme.
Expected Result: Undefined in the LLD: the pattern in section 7.3 is case-sensitive (returns 401) while RFC 7235 treats the scheme as case-insensitive. Stakeholder decision needed before asserting 200 or 401.

Title: Apply defaults for the login rate limit and token lifetime
Preconditions: Env has only the required variables (MONGODB_URI, JWT_SECRET of 32 characters, PLANT_TIME_ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')
Steps:
1. Call loadConfig without the new variables.
2. Read the result.
Expected Result: loginRateLimitMax is 5; loginRateLimitWindowMs is 900000; jwtExpiresIn is '1h'.

Title: Coerce LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX and LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS overrides to numbers
Preconditions: Valid base env plus LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX='3' and LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS='60000'
Steps:
1. Call loadConfig.
2. Check the types and values.
Expected Result: loginRateLimitMax is the number 3 and loginRateLimitWindowMs is the number 60000.

Title: Include the new variables in .env.example with placeholders only
Preconditions: Repository file .env.example (the only env file read)
Test Data: Keys LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX, LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS, ADMIN_USER_ID, ADMIN_NAME, ADMIN_PASSWORD
Steps:
1. Read .env.example.
2. Parse the key list and values.
Expected Result: All five keys are present; values are placeholders (for example 'change-me'), not real credentials; the file contains no real secret.

Title: Reject invalid LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX values naming only the variable
Steps:
1. Call loadConfig for each value.
2. Catch the error.
Expected Result: Each call throws 'Invalid configuration: LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX'; the message does not contain the supplied value.

Title: Reject invalid LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS values
Steps:
1. Call loadConfig for each value.
2. Catch the error.
Expected Result: Each call throws 'Invalid configuration: LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS' without echoing the value.

Title: Reject a missing or short JWT_SECRET without printing it
Steps:
1. Call loadConfig with the secret missing.
2. Call loadConfig with the 31-character secret.
Expected Result: Both throw 'Invalid configuration: JWT_SECRET'; the 31-character value does not appear in the message.

Title: Accept boundary values for the new settings and the secret
Test Data: LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX='1'; LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS='1000'; JWT_SECRET of exactly 32 characters
Steps: 1. Call loadConfig with each boundary value.
Expected Result: Each call succeeds; the values are 1, 1000 and the 32-character secret.

Title: Report every invalid new variable by name only
Steps:
1. Call loadConfig.
2. Catch the error.
Expected Result: The message lists LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX and LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS and contains neither 'abc' nor '5' as a value.

Title: Return a frozen config object
Steps:
1. Call loadConfig.
2. Try to assign a property.
Expected Result: The assignment throws TypeError or is ignored; loginRateLimitMax is unchanged.

Title: Accept statuses 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 429 in ValidationError
Test Data: new ValidationError([{ rule: 'UNAUTHENTICATED', message: 'A valid token is required.', fix: 'Sign in again.' }], status) for each status
Steps:
1. Construct a ValidationError for each status.
2. Read err.status.
Expected Result: No constructor throws; err.status equals the status passed.

Title: Return a 401 ValidationError in the standard contract
Steps:
1. Call the route.
2. Read status and body.
Expected Result: Status 401; body { error: 'ValidationError', failures: [{ rule: 'UNAUTHENTICATED', message: 'A valid token is required.', fix: 'Sign in again.' }] } with Content-Type JSON.

Title: Return a 429 ValidationError with details and keep the Retry-After header
Preconditions: Test route that sets Retry-After '900' then throws ValidationError 429 'RATE_LIMITED' with details { retryAfterSeconds: 900 }
Steps:
1. Call the route.
2. Read status, headers and body.
Expected Result: Status 429; header Retry-After '900'; failures[0].rule 'RATE_LIMITED' and failures[0].details.retryAfterSeconds 900.

Title: Reject unsupported ValidationError statuses
Steps: 1. Construct a ValidationError with each status.
Expected Result: Each construction throws; 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 429 remain the only accepted statuses.

Title: Keep unexpected errors as 500 INTERNAL_ERROR without a stack
Preconditions: Test route that throws Error('db down')
Steps:
1. Call the route.
2. Read the body.
Expected Result: Status 500; failures[0].rule 'INTERNAL_ERROR'; the body contains neither 'db down' nor a stack trace.

Title: Limit 401, 403 and 429 bodies to the contract fields
Preconditions: Responses from TC-042, TC-177 and TC-157
Steps:
1. Collect the three response bodies.
2. List the top-level keys and failure keys.
Expected Result: Top-level keys are exactly error and failures; each failure has only rule, message, fix and optionally details; no stack, token or user data appears.

Title: Confirm the HLD update for new statuses and rule codes
Preconditions: HLD section on the error contract lists statuses 400, 403, 409, 422 and does not list UNAUTHENTICATED, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, ACCOUNT_INACTIVE or RATE_LIMITED
Steps: 1. Compare the HLD lists with LLD section 9.
Expected Result: Pending decision (LLD OQ-03, OQ-04): the HLD must add statuses 401 and 429 and the four rule codes; tests follow the LLD until then.

Title: Return 200 with token, tokenType, expiresAt and public user for valid credentials
Preconditions: Seed users; sup01 supervisor active 'Asha Rao', password 'Correct-Horse-42'
Steps:
1. Send the request.
2. Read the body.
Expected Result: Status 200; token has three dot-separated segments; tokenType 'Bearer'; expiresAt is ISO-8601 UTC ending in 'Z'; user { userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', role: 'supervisor', status: 'active' }.

Title: Log in each of the three roles
Preconditions: Active users sup01, op01, adm01 with password 'Correct-Horse-42'
Steps:
1. Log in as sup01.
2. Log in as op01.
3. Log in as adm01.
Expected Result: Each returns 200 with user.role 'supervisor', 'operator' and 'administrator' respectively.

Title: Send Cache-Control no-store on a successful login
Steps:
1. Send the request.
2. Read the headers.
Expected Result: Header Cache-Control is 'no-store'.

Title: Normalize userId by trimming and lowercasing
Test Data: userId ' SUP01 ' and userId 'Sup01' with password 'Correct-Horse-42'
Steps:
1. Log in with ' SUP01 '.
2. Log in with 'Sup01'.
Expected Result: Both return 200 with user.userId 'sup01'.

Title: Set expiresAt to now plus JWT_EXPIRES_IN in UTC
Steps:
1. Freeze the clock.
2. Log in.
3. Compare expiresAt with the clock.

Title: Issue a JWT with only sub, iat and exp signed with HS256
Steps:
1. Log in.
2. Decode the token header and payload without verifying.
Expected Result: Header alg is 'HS256'; payload keys are exactly sub, iat and exp; sub is 'sup01'; no name, role or password claim.

Title: Accept a 72-byte password made of multi-byte characters
Preconditions: User uni01 whose password is 'é' repeated 36 times (72 bytes)
Steps: 1. Send the request.
Expected Result: Status 200 with a token.

Title: Reject a wrong password with 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS
Steps: 1. Send the request.
Expected Result: Status 401; failures[0] rule 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS', message 'The user ID or password is incorrect.', fix 'Check your user ID and password and try again.'; no token in the body.

Title: Return the same 401 body for an unknown user ID and a wrong password
Test Data: POST login { userId: 'ghost01', password: 'Correct-Horse-42' } and { userId: 'sup01', password: 'Wrong-Horse-42' }
Steps:
1. Send both requests.

1. Call the endpoint.
2. List the body keys.
Expected Result: Status 200; body keys are exactly status and timestamp; status 'ok'; timestamp is ISO-8601 UTC.

Title: Render the page for an allowed role
Preconditions: Authenticated supervisor; route element <RequireAuth roles={['supervisor']} /> with child text 'Work orders'
Steps:
1. Render the router.
2. Read the page.
Expected Result: 'Work orders' is rendered; ForbiddenView is not rendered.

Title: Render for any authenticated user when no roles prop is set
Steps: 1. Render the router.
Expected Result: The Outlet content is rendered.

Title: Return to the remembered page after login
Preconditions: Anonymous user visits '/work-orders'; login mocked to succeed
Steps:
1. Visit '/work-orders' (redirected to /login).
2. Submit valid credentials.
Expected Result: Location is '/work-orders' after login and its content is rendered.

Title: Redirect an anonymous user to /login and remember the target
Steps:
1. Render the router at '/work-orders'.
2. Read location and state.
Expected Result: Location is '/login' with state.from '/work-orders'; protected content is not rendered.

Title: Show ForbiddenView for a disallowed role
Steps:
1. Render the router.
2. Read the page.
Expected Result: ForbiddenView is rendered; 'Work orders' content is not rendered; no API call is made by the guard.

Title: Redirect an anonymous visit to the home page
Steps: 1. Render the App at '/'.
Expected Result: Location is '/login'; the home page is not rendered.

Title: Show a loading view without redirecting while status is loading
Steps: 1. Render the router.
Expected Result: A loading text is rendered; no redirect to /login and no protected content.

Title: Redirect to /login when a 401 arrives mid-session
Preconditions: Authenticated supervisor on '/'; next API call mocked to return 401
Steps:
1. Trigger the call.
2. Wait for state updates.
Expected Result: Token cleared, status 'anonymous' and location '/login'.

Title: Guard unknown paths
Preconditions: Route table with NotFoundPage and RequireAuth
Test Data: Anonymous visit to '/nope'; authenticated visit to '/nope'
Steps:
1. Visit '/nope' anonymously.
2. Visit '/nope' as sup01.
Expected Result: Anonymous: redirected to '/login'. Authenticated: NotFoundPage is rendered.

Title: Keep /login reachable for anonymous users without a redirect loop
Steps: 1. Render the App at '/login'.
Expected Result: The login form is rendered; location stays '/login'.

Title: Block protected content after logout and browser back
Preconditions: Authenticated supervisor viewed '/work-orders', then clicked Logout
Steps:
1. Log out.
2. Navigate back.
Expected Result: Location is '/login'; protected content is not rendered.

Title: Keep passwordHash and the plain password out of every response
Preconditions: Users sup01, ina01; rate limit max 4; test routes for 403 and 500
Test Data: Responses: login 200, login 401, login 403, login 400, login 429, /me 200, 401 route, 403 route
Steps:
1. Collect each response body and headers.
2. Search for 'passwordHash', '$2a$', '$2b$' and 'Correct-Horse-42'.
Expected Result: None of the strings appears in any body or header.

Title: Log no password, token or user ID
Preconditions: console.log, console.info, console.warn and console.error spied
Test Data: Successful login, failed login, 401 and 403 calls for sup01 with password 'Correct-Horse-42'
Steps:
1. Run the four calls.
2. Join all spy output.
Expected Result: The output contains none of 'Correct-Horse-42', the issued token, or 'sup01'.

Title: Keep the token only in sessionStorage
Test Data: Log in as sup01 and inspect storage, cookies and URL
Steps:
1. Log in.
2. Read sessionStorage, localStorage, document.cookie and location.
Expected Result: The token exists only under sessionStorage key 'shopfloor.token'; localStorage and cookies are empty of it; the URL has no token; the token is not rendered in the DOM.

Title: Protect every /api route except health and login by default
Preconditions: Router stack of createRoutes(config) including test routes registered after authenticate
Test Data: Enumerate registered paths and methods; call each without a token
Steps:
1. List all registered routes.
2. Call each one with no token.
Expected Result: Every route other than GET /api/health and POST /api/auth/login returns 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a forged token signed with a guessable secret
Preconditions: Token for sup01 signed with secret 'secret'
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/auth/me.
Expected Result: Status 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Give no signal that distinguishes unknown user from wrong password
Steps:
1. Send both requests.
2. Compare status, body and headers (ignoring Date and RateLimit values).
Expected Result: Status, body and headers match.

Title: Return a safe 500 and log no credentials on an unexpected login error
Preconditions: User.findOne mocked to reject Error('db down'); console.error spied
Steps:
1. Send the request.
2. Read the body and logged output.
Expected Result: Status 500 with rule 'INTERNAL_ERROR'; the body has no stack; logged output has name, message and stack only and does not contain 'Correct-Horse-42' or the request body.

Title: Return identical 401 bodies for missing, expired and tampered tokens
Test Data: Requests with no token, an expired token and a tampered token
Steps:
1. Send the three requests.
2. Compare bodies.
Expected Result: All three bodies are identical; the failure reason is not disclosed.

Title: Render a user name containing markup as plain text
Preconditions: Authenticated user with name ''
Steps:
1. Render the header.
2. Query for img elements.
Expected Result: The name is shown as literal text; no img element is created and no script runs.

Title: Stop bcrypt work once the source is limited
Test Data: 100 sequential failed logins from one source
Steps:
1. Send 100 failed logins.
2. Count verifyPassword calls.
Expected Result: verifyPassword is called at most 3 times; the remaining requests return 429 without a password comparison.

Title: Compare response times for unknown and known users
Test Data: 20 failed logins for 'ghost01' and 20 for sup01 with a wrong password (rate limit raised for the test)
Steps:
1. Time both groups.
2. Compare the medians.
Expected Result: The medians differ by less than 50 percent (best effort, LLD OQ-18).

Title: Clarify token revocation and logout limits
Preconditions: Token stolen before logout; no logout endpoint
Test Data: Use the old token after client logout
Steps:
1. Log out on the client.
2. Call GET /api/auth/me with the saved token.
Expected Result: Per LLD OQ-05 the token remains valid until expiry or user deactivation; stakeholder must accept this MVP limit or require a revocation mechanism.

Title: Create the first administrator with a bcrypt hash
Steps:
1. Call the service.
2. Read the user with +passwordHash.
Expected Result: Returns { created: true }; one user with role 'administrator', status 'active', name 'Meera Nair' and a bcrypt hash that verifies 'Seed-Password-42'.

Title: Allow the seeded administrator to log in
Steps:
1. Seed.
2. Log in through the API.
Expected Result: Status 200 with user.role 'administrator'.

Title: Normalize the seeded userId
Test Data: seedAdministrator({ userId: ' ADMIN01 ', name: 'Meera Nair', password: 'Seed-Password-42' })
Steps:
1. Seed.
2. Read the stored userId.
Expected Result: Stored userId is 'admin01'.

Title: Report creation from the seed script
Preconditions: Test env ADMIN_USER_ID='admin01', ADMIN_NAME='Meera Nair', ADMIN_PASSWORD='Seed-Password-42'; empty test database
Steps:
1. Run the script.
2. Read exit code and output.
Expected Result: Exit code 0; output 'Administrator created.'; the database connection closes; output does not contain the password.

Title: Report an existing administrator from the seed script
Preconditions: An administrator already exists; same env variables
Steps:
1. Run the script.
2. Read exit code, output and users.
Expected Result: Exit code 0; output 'An administrator already exists; nothing changed.'; no user added or changed.

Title: Stop when a required seed variable is missing
Preconditions: Env with one of ADMIN_USER_ID, ADMIN_NAME, ADMIN_PASSWORD removed at a time
Steps:
1. Run with ADMIN_USER_ID missing.
2. Run with ADMIN_NAME missing.
3. Run with ADMIN_PASSWORD missing.
Expected Result: Each run exits with code 1; output names only the missing variable; no user is created.

Title: Reject an ADMIN_PASSWORD shorter than 12 characters
Test Data: Run the seed env parser / script
Steps:
1. Run with the short password.
2. Read output and users.
Expected Result: Exit code 1; output names ADMIN_PASSWORD only and does not print its value; no user created.

Title: Change nothing when another administrator exists
Preconditions: Administrator adm01 exists with a known hash
Steps:
1. Call the service.
2. Count users and compare adm01's hash.
Expected Result: Returns { created: false }; no user 'admin02'; adm01 unchanged.

Title: Not overwrite an existing non-administrator with the same userId
Preconditions: User sup01 (supervisor) exists; no administrator exists
Steps:
1. Call the service.
2. Read sup01.
Expected Result: Returns { created: false } (duplicate key 11000); sup01 keeps role 'supervisor', name and password hash; no administrator created.

Title: Exit 1 with a generic message on a database error
Preconditions: MongoDB unreachable (invalid test URI placeholder); valid seed env
Steps:
1. Run the script.
2. Read exit code and output.
Expected Result: Exit code 1; a generic error message; no stack leaking the password; the password value is not printed.

Title: Reject a 65-character ADMIN_USER_ID
Preconditions: Empty users collection; ADMIN_USER_ID of 65 characters
Steps:
1. Run the script.
2. Count users.
Expected Result: Exit code 1; no user created; output does not contain the password.

Title: Accept an ADMIN_PASSWORD of exactly 12 characters
Steps: 1. Run the script.
Expected Result: Exit code 0; 'Administrator created.'.

Title: Reject empty and whitespace-only seed variables
Steps: 1. Run the script.
Expected Result: Exit code 1; output names the failing variables only; no user created.

Title: Be idempotent on a repeated service call
Preconditions: Administrator created by a first call
Test Data: seedAdministrator with the same values a second time
Steps:
1. Call the service twice.
2. Count users and compare the hash.
Expected Result: First call { created: true }; second { created: false }; one user; hash unchanged.

Title: Create exactly one administrator for two parallel seed calls
Test Data: Two simultaneous seedAdministrator calls with the same values
Steps:
1. Run both with Promise.all.
2. Count users.
Expected Result: Exactly one result has created true; the other created false; one document exists; no error is thrown.

Title: Never print the password in any seed script path
Preconditions: Spy on stdout and stderr; run success, existing-admin, invalid-env and database-error paths
Steps:
1. Run each path.
2. Search all captured output.
Expected Result: 'Seed-Password-42' appears in no output.

Title: Clarify handling of a seed password over 72 bytes
Test Data: Run the script with the 80-character password
Steps:
1. Run the script.
2. Try login with the first 72 bytes only.
Expected Result: LLD requires at least 12 characters for the seed but the login schema rejects over 72 bytes and bcrypt truncates silently; the maximum for ADMIN_PASSWORD is undefined. Confirm the rule.

Title: Round trip sign and verify with only sub, iat and exp
Preconditions: Config with a 32-character test secret; jwtExpiresIn '1h'
Steps:
1. Sign the token.
2. Verify it.
3. List the payload keys.
Expected Result: verifyToken returns a payload with sub 'sup01', iat and exp; keys are exactly sub, iat, exp.

Title: Sign with HS256 and a 1 hour lifetime
Steps:
1. Sign the token.
2. Decode header and payload.
Expected Result: Header alg 'HS256'; exp minus iat equals 3600.

Title: Honor a configured lifetime of 15 minutes
Steps:
1. Sign the token.
2. Decode the payload.
Expected Result: exp minus iat equals 900.

Title: Reject an expired token
Steps: 1. Call verifyToken.
Expected Result: Throws ValidationError 401 with rule 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a tampered signature
Preconditions: Valid token with its signature changed
Steps: 1. Call verifyToken.
Expected Result: Throws ValidationError 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject alg none
Steps: 1. Call verifyToken.
Expected Result: Throws ValidationError 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject a token signed with another secret
Steps: 1. Call verifyToken.
Expected Result: Throws ValidationError 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject HS512 even with the correct secret
Preconditions: Token signed with algorithm HS512 and the correct secret
Steps: 1. Call verifyToken.
Expected Result: Throws ValidationError 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED' (algorithms pinned to HS256).

Title: Reject a non-string subject
Preconditions: Correctly signed tokens with sub values { $ne: null }, ['sup01'], 123 and null
Steps: 1. Call verifyToken with each token.
Expected Result: Each call throws ValidationError 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Reject garbage input
Steps: 1. Call verifyToken with each input.
Expected Result: Each call throws ValidationError 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'; never a raw jsonwebtoken error.

Title: Reject a token whose nbf is in the future
Steps: 1. Call verifyToken.
Expected Result: Throws ValidationError 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Switch from valid to invalid at the expiry second
Preconditions: Fake timers; token with expiresIn '1s' issued at 2026-01-05T09:00:00Z
Steps:
1. Verify at the first time.
2. Verify at the second time.
Expected Result: First call returns the payload; second throws ValidationError 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

Title: Use the same error text for every failure reason
Steps:
1. Catch each error.
2. Compare failures.
Expected Result: Every error has message 'A valid token is required.' and fix 'Sign in again.'.

Title: Accept an empty-string subject in verifyToken and let the lookup fail
Steps:
1. Call verifyToken.
2. Call getUserForToken.
Expected Result: verifyToken returns the payload (the subject is a string); getUserForToken throws 401 'UNAUTHENTICATED' because no user matches.

Title: Clarify handling of a correctly signed token without exp
Preconditions: Token signed with the correct secret and HS256 but no expiresIn option
Steps: 1. Call verifyToken.
Expected Result: LLD says verification checks expiry and tokens expire after JWT_EXPIRES_IN, but the pseudocode does not require an exp claim; a token without exp would never expire. Confirm whether to reject it.

Title: Store and read the token under shopfloor.token
Steps:
1. Call setToken.
2. Call getToken.
3. Read sessionStorage directly.
Expected Result: getToken returns 'tok-abc'; sessionStorage key 'shopfloor.token' holds 'tok-abc'.

Title: Remove the token with clearToken
Steps:
1. Call clearToken.
2. Call getToken.
Expected Result: getToken returns null; the sessionStorage key is gone.

Title: Return null when no token is stored
Steps: 1. Call getToken.
Expected Result: Returns null (not undefined or an empty string).

Title: Overwrite an existing token and leave localStorage unused
Steps:
1. Call setToken with the new value.
2. Read both storages.
Expected Result: getToken returns 'tok-new'; localStorage contains no shopfloor.token.

Title: Not throw when clearing an empty store
Steps: 1. Call clearToken twice.
Expected Result: No exception; getToken returns null.

Title: Create a valid user with defaults and timestamps
Test Data: User.create({ userId: 'sup01', name: 'Asha Rao', passwordHash: '$2a$04$hashvalue', role: 'supervisor' })
Steps:
1. Create the user.
2. Read the stored document.
Expected Result: status defaults to 'active'; createdAt and updatedAt are Date values; userId 'sup01'.

Title: Trim and lowercase userId and trim name
Steps:
1. Create the user.
2. Read the stored values.
Expected Result: userId 'sup01'; name 'Asha Rao'.

Title: Accept every role and status value
Test Data: roles supervisor, operator, administrator; statuses active, inactive
Steps:
1. Create one user per role.
2. Create one user per status.
Expected Result: All creations succeed; ROLES and USER_STATUSES export the same values.

Title: Exclude passwordHash from queries by default
Steps:
1. Query without select.
2. Query with +passwordHash.
Expected Result: First result has no passwordHash; second result has it.

Title: Drop passwordHash and __v in toJSON
Steps: 1. Serialize the document.
Expected Result: The JSON contains no passwordHash and no __v.

Title: Create a unique index on userId
Steps: 1. Read the index list.
Expected Result: An index on { userId: 1 } with unique true exists.

Title: Reject a user missing a required field
Test Data: Four creations each missing one of userId, name, passwordHash, role
Steps: 1. Try each creation.
Expected Result: Each fails with a Mongoose ValidationError naming the missing path.

Title: Reject an invalid role
Steps: 1. Try each creation.
Expected Result: Each fails with a ValidationError on role; no document saved.

Title: Reject an invalid status
Steps: 1. Try the creation.
Expected Result: Fails with a ValidationError on status.

Title: Reject a duplicate userId including a case variant
Steps: 1. Try both creations.
Expected Result: Both fail with duplicate key error code 11000.

Title: Reject whitespace-only userId and name
Steps: 1. Try each creation.
Expected Result: Each fails with a ValidationError (required after trim).

Title: Reject an operator object as userId on create
Steps: 1. Try the creation.
Expected Result: Fails with a cast ValidationError; no document is stored.

Title: Enforce userId length 64
Steps:
1. Create with 64 characters.
2. Create with 65 characters.
Expected Result: 64 characters succeeds; 65 characters fails with a ValidationError.

Title: Enforce name length 100
Steps:
1. Create with 100 characters.
2. Create with 101 characters.
Expected Result: 100 characters succeeds; 101 characters fails with a ValidationError.

Title: Keep sanitizeFilter on so operators are not interpreted
Steps: 1. Run the query.
Expected Result: The operator is not applied: the result is null or the query is rejected; sup01 is not returned.

Title: Create one user when 5 parallel creates share a userId
Steps:
1. Run them with Promise.allSettled.
2. Count fulfilled results and documents.
Expected Result: Exactly 1 fulfilled; 4 rejected with code 11000; one document stored.
